claims.text: The starting catalyst is a multi-element automotive alloy containing multiple principal elements in nearly equiatomic ratios.
The starting catalyst has a low platinum-group-metal loading.
The proposed intervention is deposition of an approximately 2–3 nm ceria overcoat by atomic layer deposition.
ALD will produce a uniform, conformal ultrathin ceria layer on the catalyst.
The ceria layer will provide dynamic oxygen storage.
The ceria layer will act as a physical barrier against sintering.
Mobile oxygen supplied by ceria will facilitate redox reactions at lower temperatures.
The ceria overcoat will physically protect underlying alloy active sites from sintering.
The ceria overcoat will protect underlying alloy active sites from chemical poisoning.
The combined oxygen-storage and protective functions will maintain catalytic performance under transient thermal and chemical exhaust stresses.
The ALD-treated catalyst will have a lower light-off temperature than the untreated catalyst.
The ALD-treated catalyst will have higher pollutant conversion efficiency, including NOx conversion, than the untreated catalyst.
The ALD-treated catalyst will undergo less performance degradation after prolonged thermal aging than the untreated catalyst.
The untreated starting catalyst exhibits progressive activity loss and durability limitations under the specified operating conditions.
The intervention will not increase platinum-group-metal usage.
The benefits may depend on the ceria layer being sufficiently uniform and optimally thin.
